name: Vocabulary Age Profile
description: Analyzes the historical depth and the psycholinguistic 'Age of Acquisition' (AoA) of the vocabulary used in a text. Large Language Models are predominantly trained on modern internet data (post-2000s web scrapes, social media, recent digital archives). Consequently, their default writing style is heavily biased toward contemporary, modernized vocabulary. Unless explicitly prompted to adopt a historical persona, AI rarely utilizes nuanced, slightly dated, or archaic terminology organically. Furthermore, humans acquire vocabulary progressively from childhood to adulthood (measured by AoA metrics), leading to semantic clusters reflective of human cognitive development. AI possesses no biological age; it treats a word learned by a 5-year-old and a word learned by a PhD student merely as different token probabilities, often mixing them in mathematically uniform ways that contradict natural human lexical profiling.
mechanism: The algorithm cross-references every word in the document against two massive linguistic databases: historical n-gram corpora (like Google Books Ngram Viewer) to determine the historical usage epoch of the word, and psycholinguistic AoA databases to determine the average human learning age. It plots the 'historical depth' and the 'developmental age' distribution of the text. A text that is ruthlessly anchored to post-2010s internet terminology, completely devoid of slightly dated organic expressions, and demonstrating an unnatural 'flat' distribution of Age-of-Acquisition words, strongly correlates with machine synthesis optimized for contemporary token generation.
useCase: Highly effective for analyzing literature, long-form journalism, historical analysis, and academic writing. It excels at detecting AI that attempts to simulate the writing of mature, highly read human experts by exposing its lack of true historical lexical depth.
strengths:
• Targets the fundamental training data bias of LLMs: their overwhelming diet of modern, highly optimized internet text.
• Psycholinguistic profiling (AoA) is nearly impossible to bypass via prompting, as prompt engineers cannot easily instruct an LLM to 'use words typically acquired by humans between ages 12 and 15'.
limitations:
• Susceptible to false positives when analyzing genuine modern content inherently constrained to new terminology, such as cryptocurrency whitepapers, recent tech blogs, or modern pop-culture reviews.
• Less effective on very short content where statistical age profiling cannot build a reliable distribution curve.
parameters:
Analysis: Diachronic Corpora Mapping & Psycholinguistic Database Matching
Metric: Contemporary Bias Ratio & AoA Generative Variance
Output: 0-100 Lexical Artificiality & Temporal Flattening Score
accuracy: High — 72-87% accuracy. It is a deeply incisive semantic feature that operates on psycholinguistic and historical levels, making it exceptionally difficult for current-generation autoregressive models to organically circumvent.

references.title: Kuperman, V. et al. (2012). Age-of-Acquisition Ratings for 30,000 English Words. Behavior Research Methods.
Brysbaert, M. et al. (2014). Concreteness Ratings for 40,000 English Lemmas. Behavior Research Methods.
